jobs.title: Senior Managing Director, Healthcare Disputes & Economics, Payer/Provider
jobs.excerpt: Ankura is a team of excellence founded on innovation and growth.
jobs.description:
Ankura is a team of excellence founded on innovation and growth.

Practice Overview:

Ankura’s Health Care team is a recognized leader in health care and life sciences disputes, compliance, and investigations. The team combines clinical, technical, operational, financial, economic, and analytic expertise to help clients and counsel resolve complex matters involving payers, providers, pharmacies, and law firms.

This role is specifically focused on expanding Ankura’s payer/provider disputes platform: matters where commercial, Medicare Advantage, Medicaid managed care, exchange, and other health plan arrangements require rigorous data analytics and defensible damages analysis.

Role Overview:

The Senior Managing Director will be an executive-level, self-sustaining rainmaker who originates, sells, leads, and testifies in complex healthcare commercial disputes. The role requires a credible marketplace presence with health plans, law firms, and healthcare-focused private equity or strategic stakeholders.

  • Primary focus: payer/provider contract, payment, reimbursement, claims, coding, utilization, medical policy, network, and financial disputes.

  • Core technical differentiator: ability to direct large-scale data analytics teams and translate complex healthcare datasets into clear, supportable damages opinions.

  • Expected revenue impact: proven, tangible business development record with the ability to produce at least $3M in revenue and a target opportunity to generate $3M to $5M+ annually.

  • Expert role: serve as a consulting expert or testifying expert, including report development, deposition preparation, arbitration or trial testimony, and expert rebuttal work.

Target Candidate Profile:

  • Market position: Recognized rainmaker in healthcare disputes with established relationships among payer/provider counsel, managed care executives, provider finance leaders, and litigation decision-makers.

  • Dispute focus: Deep experience in payer/provider commercial disputes, including underpayment, overpayment, contract interpretation, rate methodology, coding, claim adjudication, stop-loss, risk adjustment, value-based care, network adequacy, medical necessity, utilization, denial, recoupment, and reimbursement disputes.

  • Data analytics leadership: Can lead multidisciplinary teams analyzing large claims, eligibility, encounter, remittance, contract, provider, authorization, utilization, coding, clinical, and financial datasets using scalable, quality-controlled analytics.

  • Damages expertise: Can develop defensible models for lost revenue, underpayment, overpayment, offsets, recoupments, interest, damages scenarios, counterfactuals, and sensitivity analyses.

  • Expert witness credibility: Has authored expert reports and provided deposition, arbitration, trial, or hearing testimony in healthcare disputes.

Responsibilities:

Business Development and Market Leadership

  • Originate and expand relationships with national and regional law firms, health plans, pharmacy organizations, and healthcare investors that routinely face payer/provider reimbursement and damages disputes.

  • Develop a go-to-market plan focused on payer/provider disputes where Ankura can combine healthcare industry expertise, advanced analytics, damages modeling, and expert testimony.

  • Build a visible marketplace presence through panels, publications, law firm briefings, client training, and industry events focused on managed care litigation, reimbursement disputes, and claims analytics.

  • Convert marketplace relationships into consulting expert, testifying expert, privileged advisory, and complex analytics engagements.

Technical and Disputes Expertise

  • Lead matters involving contract breaches, payment disputes, underpayment or overpayment claims, reimbursement methodology, fee schedules, DRG/APC/APG or other payment logic, risk corridors, value-based payment, capitation, shared savings, risk adjustment, denials, recoupments, and claims adjudication issues.

  • Apply knowledge of commercial, Medicare Advantage, Part D, Medicaid managed care, ACA exchange, pharmacy, and provider reimbursement operations when developing case strategy and damages approaches.

  • Assess liability and damages theories in collaboration with counsel while preserving attorney-client privilege, work-product protection, and expert independence where applicable.

  • Prepare expert reports, rebuttal reports, declarations, deposition testimony, arbitration testimony, trial testimony, and demonstratives that explain complex analytics in plain English.

Large-Scale Data Analytics and Damages

  • Direct data teams analyzing high-volume healthcare datasets, including claims, encounters, eligibility, premium, membership, remittance, EOB/EOP, authorization, denial, utilization, coding, provider contract, fee schedule, capitation, risk adjustment, and financial data.

  • Design repeatable analytic workplans that include data intake, normalization, validation, completeness testing, reconciliation, exception handling, sampling or extrapolation where appropriate, quality control, and audit trails.

  • Develop damages models that quantify alleged underpayments, overpayments, lost revenue, leakage, offsets, recoupment exposure, reasonable value, contract-based damages, and alternative damages scenarios.

  • Translate analytic findings into counsel-ready narratives, executive presentations, settlement support, mediation materials, expert reports, and trial or arbitration demonstratives.

  • Partner with data scientists, statisticians, coding experts, clinicians, economists, forensic accountants, and operations professionals to ensure analytic conclusions are technically sound and legally defensible.

Client Delivery and Team Leadership

  • Serve as the accountable executive on complex, multi-workstream matters with law firm, payer, provider, and board-level stakeholders.

  • Scope and price engagements, staff teams, manage budgets, review work product, ensure quality, and deliver concise insights under litigation deadlines.

  • Mentor directors, managing directors, analytics professionals, clinicians, coders, and operational specialists, with a focus on developing future testifying experts and client-facing leaders.

  • Collaborate across Ankura practices, including Health Economics, Data Analytics including AI, Strategy and Performance, Forensic Accounting, Investigations, and other dispute capabilities.

Relevant Matter Experience

  • Payer/provider contract disputes involving alleged underpayment, denial, repricing, reimbursement methodology, rate implementation, or recoupment issues.

  • Managed care disputes involving Medicare Advantage, Medicaid managed care, ACA exchange, commercial group, self-funded, pharmacy, or delegated-risk arrangements.

  • Large-scale claims and encounter analytics supporting affirmative damages, rebuttal damages, settlement valuation, mediation, arbitration, or trial.

  • Hospital, physician, ancillary, pharmacy, behavioral health, and specialty provider reimbursement disputes.

  • Matters requiring expert reports, rebuttal analyses, deposition testimony, arbitration testimony, or trial testimony.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited university in business, finance, accounting, economics, data analytics, health care operations, health policy, clinical discipline, or a related field; advanced degree preferred.

  • 10+ years of litigation, disputes, forensic, damages, payer/provider reimbursement, managed care, healthcare analytics, or consulting experience; senior consulting leadership experience strongly preferred.

  • Proven and tangible business development record with a portable book of relationships and revenue generation of at least $3M; demonstrated ability to grow toward $3M to $5M+ annually.

  • Specific experience originating and leading payer/provider commercial disputes, reimbursement disputes, managed care litigation, claims analytics, damages quantification, or expert witness engagements.

  • Demonstrated ability to direct large project teams analyzing complex healthcare datasets and producing quality-controlled analytic outputs for counsel, executives, and triers of fact.

  • Experience authoring expert reports, rebuttal reports, declarations, affidavits, or damages analyses; prior deposition, arbitration, trial, or hearing testimony strongly preferred.

  • Strong understanding of healthcare legal, regulatory, reimbursement, and operational issues affecting payers, providers, pharmacies, and government program participants.

  • Exceptional executive communication skills, including the ability to explain complex technical, analytic, reimbursement, and damages issues to boards, C-suite clients, law firms, regulators, mediators, arbitrators, judges, and juries.

  • Demonstrated commitment to privilege, confidentiality, work-product discipline, expert independence, collaboration, quality, and team development.

  • Ability and willingness to travel; must be legally authorized to work in the United States without employer sponsorship now or in the future.

Position Summary

The Epilepsy Foundation is seeking a detail-oriented and strategic Senior Manager of Contracts and Procurement with deep experience in government grant compliance, contract negotiation, procurement, and regulatory reporting within the nonprofit sector.

This role is responsible for overseeing the organization’s contracts and procurement functions while ensuring compliance with federal, state, and local requirements, including the Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act (FFATA), Uniform Guidance (2 CFR Part 200), and applicable state charitable registration requirements.

The ideal candidate will have demonstrated experience navigating complex regulatory requirements, managing high-stakes contracts and agreements, and partnering across departments to mitigate organizational risk and ensure compliance. This position will serve as a key subject matter expert on grant-related procurement, contracting, and regulatory obligations while supporting the Foundation’s mission and organizational priorities.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Contracts & Procurement Management: Execute and oversee the end-to-end contracts and procurement function, with a strong focus on regulatory compliance for federally and state-funded grants.
  • Federal Grant Compliance: Ensure organizational adherence to federal grant requirements, including FFATA reporting, Uniform Guidance (2 CFR Part 200), cost principles, procurement standards, and other applicable requirements.
  • Contract Development & Negotiation: Lead the review, drafting, negotiation, and administration of contracts, memoranda of understanding (MOUs), subrecipient agreements, cooperative agreements, and vendor contracts.
  • Charitable Registration Compliance: Coordinate state charitable solicitation registrations, renewals, and related compliance requirements across applicable jurisdictions.
  • Policies & Procedures: Develop, implement, maintain, and continuously improve procurement and contracting policies and procedures that align with nonprofit best practices and regulatory requirements.
  • Grant & Funder Requirements: Monitor and report on compliance with funder-specific procurement requirements, contractual obligations, and reporting requirements.
  • Subject Matter Expertise: Serve as the organization’s subject matter expert on grant-related procurement, contracting requirements, and regulatory obligations.
  • Cross-Functional Partnership: Partner closely with Legal, Finance, Programs, Development, and other internal stakeholders to align procurement and contracting activities with organizational goals, grant requirements, and deliverables.
  • Vendor & Subcontractor Management: Manage supplier, vendor, subcontractor, and subrecipient due diligence, contractual obligations, compliance requirements, and performance.
  • Audit Support: Play an integral role in organizational audits, including the annual Uniform Guidance Audit, by ensuring appropriate procurement and contracting documentation and compliance.
  • Training & Guidance: Develop and provide training and guidance to internal stakeholders on procurement compliance, contracting procedures, ethics, and federal and state funding requirements.
  • Risk Management: Identify and mitigate contractual, procurement, and compliance risks while ensuring appropriate documentation and internal controls.
  • Process Improvement: Identify opportunities to strengthen contracting and procurement processes, improve operational efficiency, and enhance organizational compliance.

Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Law, Public Administration, Business Administration, Finance, or a related field required; JD or master’s degree preferred.
  • Minimum of 8–10 years of progressive experience in contract management and procurement, including at least 5 years supporting federal and state grant compliance within a nonprofit, government, or government-funded environment.
  • In-depth knowledge of FFATA, 2 CFR Part 200 (Uniform Guidance), federal procurement requirements, cost principles, and state charitable registration requirements.
  • Demonstrated experience managing complex grant-related contracts, subrecipient agreements, cooperative agreements, subcontracts, and vendor relationships.
  • Strong contract drafting, review, negotiation, and risk assessment skills.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of procurement regulations, internal controls, audit readiness, and compliance requirements applicable to nonprofits and federal grantees.
  • Experience supporting organizational audits, including Uniform Guidance Audits.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, problem-solving, and project management skills.
  • Ability to interpret complex regulatory and contractual requirements and communicate them clearly to internal stakeholders.
  • Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively across Legal, Finance, Programs, Development, and other organizational functions.
  • Ability to manage multiple complex priorities and deadlines while maintaining strong attention to detail.
  • Demonstrated ability to exercise sound judgment, discretion, and ethical decision-making.
  • Proficiency with contract, grant, financial, and organizational management systems; experience with Salesforce and Sage Intacct preferred.

Key Competencies:

  • Regulatory & Compliance Expertise
  • Contract Drafting & Negotiation
  • Federal & State Grant Compliance
  • Nonprofit Legal & Regulatory Acumen
  • Procurement & Vendor Management
  • Risk Assessment & Mitigation
  • Attention to Detail
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration
  • Strategic Thinking & Process Improvement

ChildFund Australia is a member of the ChildFund Alliance – a global network of 10 organisations which assists almost 36 million children and their families in 66 countries. ChildFund Australia directly manages and implements programs with a range of local partners in Cambodia, Myanmar, Papua New Guinea, Timor-Leste, Vietnam, and other Pacific nations, and manages projects delivered by partner organisations throughout Asia, Africa, and the Americas.

ChildFund seeks to strengthen its existing participation approach so that stakeholders can engage with, validate, challenge, and enrich the findings of Child Rights Situation Analyses, helping to identify priority issues, emerging trends, evidence gaps, and opportunities for action. The resulting insights will inform organisational strategy, country planning, program portfolios, advocacy priorities, and investment decisions, ensuring that these are grounded not only in published evidence but also in the perspectives and experiences of children and communities themselves.

This assignment will develop practical guidelines, tools, and supporting resources that enable this process to be undertaken consistently across country contexts. The approach should be low burden, repeatable, and designed to leverage existing community engagement structures wherever possible, recognising the capacity constraints facing Country Offices and partners. It should also promote accountability by establishing clear mechanisms for reporting back on how participant feedback influenced findings, priorities, and subsequent decisions.

The consultant will also provide technical advice on the role of Youth Voice in ChildFund’s strategy development and broader strategic decision-making, including its evolving purpose, Terms of Reference, engagement processes and feedback mechanisms.

The consultancy period is 20 days spread across 3 months.

Interested consultants should submit an expression of interest including: a technical proposal (max. 3 pages) outlining understanding of the assignment, proposed search strategy and sources, and workplan; a financial proposal/fee schedule in USD; a curriculum vitae including at least two references from similar assignments; and a sample of previous, similar written work.

We take extensive steps to safeguard children in any work done by our people, i.e., our staff, volunteers and interns, supporters, partners, board members, ambassadors and suppliers. As part of this commitment, all people working with us will undergo relevant background checks before joining ChildFund Australia.

We’re building a world of health around every individual — shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger – helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time.

Do you have a passion for engaging with people and helping them on their journey to better health? Signify Health, part of CVS Health®, is seeking a Full Time Physician to provide In-Home Health Evaluations, engaging with people in the comfort of their own homes and helping bridge gaps in care.

You’ll play a critical role in building trusted relationships to make people healthier, helping bring flexible, comprehensive and personalized health evaluations right to people’s front doors.

Job highlights

The visit, which lasts about 45 minutes, allows for time to connect one-on-one and answer health questions. It includes a medication and medical history review, a physical evaluation, and, if ordered by the person’s health plan, additional diagnostic tests (i.e., diabetic eye exams, spirometry, etc.). You’ll use an iPad and an intuitive clinical workflow for each evaluation and are not required to prescribe medicine, order lab tests or alter people’s current treatment regimen.

In this role, you will:

  • Bring your heart into every visit, joining a national network of purpose-driven clinicians dedicated to improving health outcomes

  • Be part of our efforts to visit millions of people nationwide with the goal of providing connections to the right care for people’s unique needs

  • Work with Signify Health as a clinician colleague, fulfilling the requirements of the specified role

  • Be flexible to travel locally and within licensed states, as needed

  • Conduct virtual visits as needed

  • Provide all Signify Health services as indicated including Diagnostic & Preventive Services products (i.e., spirometry, DEE, bone density screening, etc.)

A Note on Our Work Environment:
As an in-home clinician, your primary workplace is the private residence of health plan members. We are dedicated to meeting health plan members where they are, wherever they call home. These environments are diverse and may present a variety of conditions. Candidates must be able to comfortably and safely perform their duties in homes that may contain household pets, secondhand smoke and other potential airborne allergens or irritants.

Why Clinicians Enjoy Working with Signify Health
“Many of the people I see are shocked that a physician is coming to their home to visit with them one-on-one. When you sit down and have an unhurried conversation about their health, they are impressed, happy, and understand that their health plan and care team cares about them.” - M.L., MD

“The primary care physician gets a snapshot of a person in an office setting, but with Signify Health, we see things like the number of steps to enter their home, the state of disrepair those steps may be in, and the person’s ability to function comfortably and with ease in their own home. We can make referrals to the individual’s health plan, encourage the participation of their loved ones, and ensure their PCPs are aware of their health and overall quality of life.” - C.H., MD

Full-time employees qualify for our comprehensive benefits package, including:

  • Health, dental and vision insurance

  • Paid time off

  • Annual CEU allowance

  • 401K

  • Supplies and other perks

Job Title: Sales Representative – Infectious Disease I Region Bayreuth, Regensburg,

Über Abbott

Abbott ist ein weltweit führendes Unternehmen im Gesundheitswesen, das bahnbrechende wissenschaftliche Erkenntnisse nutzt und Lösungen zur Verbesserung der Gesundheit der Menschen entwickelt. Wir blicken stets in die Zukunft und antizipieren Veränderungen in der medizinischen Wissenschaft und Technologie.

In Deutschland ist Abbott mit mehr als 4.000 Mitarbeiter:innen in den Bereichen Forschung und Entwicklung, Logistik, Produktion und Vertrieb vertreten. Neben dem deutschen Hauptsitz in Wiesbaden hat Abbott Standorte in Hannover, Neustadt am Rübenberge, Wetzlar, Eschborn, Jena, Köln und Hamburg.

 

Die Position

Die Position wird an unserem Standort Köln (Abbott Rapid Diagnostics Germany GmbH) im Bereich Infectious Diseases angegliedert und für die Region Bayreuth, Regensburg, Rosenheimverantwortlich sein.

Unser Point-of-Care-Diagnoseportfolio umfasst wichtige Gesundheits- und Therapiebereiche, darunter Infektionskrankheiten, kardiometabolische und Toxikologie.

Unsere diagnostischen Lösungen werden in Krankenhäusern, Laboren und Kliniken rund um den Globus eingesetzt. Die entscheidenden Informationen, die aus unseren Tests, Instrumenten und Informatiksystemen gewonnen werden, sind oft der erste Schritt bei der Entscheidungsfindung in der Patientenversorgung für Hunderte von Gesundheitszuständen, von Herzinfarkten über Blutkrankheiten bis hin zu Infektionskrankheiten und Krebs.

Unsere schnellen Diagnoselösungen tragen dazu bei, einige der größten Herausforderungen der Welt im Gesundheitswesen zu bewältigen.

Ihre Aufgaben

  • Eigenverantwortliche Steuerung der Vertriebsziele sowie der kommerziellen Planung zur nachhaltigen Erreichung der Leistungsziele in Ihrer Region
  • Aktive Marktbearbeitung und Kundenentwicklung mit Fokus auf Neukundengewinnung sowie langfristige Betreuung und Ausbau bestehender Kundenbeziehungen
  • Verantwortung für die strategische Entwicklung und erfolgreiche Umsetzung des Abbott RDx ID‑Produktportfolios im definierten Vertriebsgebiet
  • Erstellung maßgeschneiderter Angebote, eigenständige Vertragsverhandlungen sowie erfolgreicher Abschluss von Kundenverträgen
  • Beobachtung, Analyse und Reporting von Wettbewerbsaktivitäten, inkl. Ableitung geeigneter Vertriebs‑ und Marktstrategien
  • Durchführung von Produktschulungen, Produktdemonstrationen und Implementierungen bei Kunden vor Ort in der Region
  • Repräsentation von Abbott auf nationalen und internationalen Kongressen, Messen und Fachveranstaltungen

Erforderliche Qualifikationen

  • Abgeschlossenes Studium der Naturwissenschaften, alternativ eine medizinische Ausbildung oder vergleichbare Berufserfahrung im Bereich Diagnostik
  • Ausgeprägte Kommunikations- und Verhandlungsstärke sowie sicheres Auftreten gegenüber klinischen Ansprechpartnern
  • Hohe Überzeugungskraft und Fähigkeit, nachhaltige Kundenbeziehungen aufzubauen und weiterzuentwickeln
  • Ergebnisorientierte, strukturierte und resiliente Arbeitsweise in einem dynamischen Umfeld
  • Stark ausgeprägte Problemlösungs- und Kundenorientierung
  • Teamorientierte Persönlichkeit mit hoher Eigeninitiative, Energie und Begeisterungsfähigkeit
  • Sehr gute Organisations‑, Präsentations‑ und Moderationsfähigkeiten
  • Sicherer Umgang mit Excel und PowerPoint
  • Hohe Reisebereitschaft (ca. 70–80 %) innerhalb des Vertriebsgebiets
  • Fließende Deutsch - sowie sehr gute Englischkenntnisse

Bevorzugte Qualifikationen

  • Mindestens 3 Jahre Berufserfahrung im Vertrieb der Medizintechnik‑, Diagnostik‑ oder Pharmaindustrie
  • Gutes Verständnis des Secondary‑Care‑ bzw. Klinikmarktes
  • Unternehmerisches Mindset, Flexibilität und Freude an der Arbeit in einem sich wandelnden Marktumfeld
  • Souveräne, wirksame Kommunikationsfähigkeit auf allen Entscheidungsebenen
  • Fähigkeit, Kundenbedarfe und Geschäftspotenziale klar zu analysieren, zu adressieren und in langfristige strategische Partnerschaften zu überführen – auch mit Kunden von nationaler Bedeutung

Haben wir Ihr Interesse geweckt? Dann bewerben Sie sich bei uns.  

Wir freuen uns auf Sie! 

Arbeiten bei Abbott

Bei Abbott finden Sie eine Aufgabe, die wirklich zählt, denn Sie verhelfen anderen Menschen zu einem gesünderen und erfüllten Leben. Wachsen Sie mit uns und lernen Sie stetig dazu – Sie können hier Ihre persönliche und berufliche Entwicklung vorantreiben und sich selbst verwirklichen.

Das erwartet Sie bei uns:

  • Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten in einem internationalen Unternehmen, in dem Sie die Karriere machen können, von der Sie träumen
  • Ein attraktives Benefit-Paket (z.B. Company Bike, Mitarbeiteraktienkaufprogramm)
  • Eine herausfordernde Position in einer schnell wachsenden krisenunabhängigen Branche
  • Die Möglichkeit, Teil eines dynamischen, hochqualifizierten und motivierten Teams zu werden
  • Flache Hierarchien, offene, wertschätzende Mentalität und effiziente, konstruktive Kommunikationswege
  • Ein multinationales Umfeld, in dem wir die Entwicklung unserer Talente innerhalb des Unternehmens fördern
  • Ein Unternehmen, das als eine der “Best Big Companies To Work For“ anerkannt ist, sowie als bester Platz zum Arbeiten für Vielfalt, arbeitende Mütter, weibliche Führungskräfte und Wissenschaftler:innen

Folgen Sie Ihren Karrierezielen bei Abbott für vielfältige Möglichkeiten mit einem Unternehmen, das Ihnen helfen kann, Ihre Zukunft aufzubauen und Ihr bestes Leben zu führen. Abbott ist ein Arbeitgeber für Chancengleichheit, der sich der Vielfalt der Mitarbeiter verschrieben hat.

  • Forte capacité d’adaptation et autonomie.
  • Esprit d’équipe et sens de l’écoute.
  • Intérêt pour les valeurs de minimalisme, nature, et bien-être.

Les bonus :

  • Parler anglais couramment est un avantage, mais non obligatoire.

Nous cherchons avant tout une personne qui souhaites lors de ce stage non rémunéré de 2 mois, apprendre de nouvelles choses ou s'offrir une opportunité au sein de notre future start-Up puisque si la personne en question travail bien, elle pourra naturellement se qualifier pour un futur poste en CDI dès lors que nous lèverons les fonds pour notre société. PS : Futur poste de directeur marketing à la clés pour les plus ambitieux ou travailleur.

Informations contractuelles

Nous sommes une startup en démarrage, bâtissant les fondations d’un projet ambitieux et visionnaire. Partir de zéro est un défi que nous relevons chaque jour avec passion et détermination. Nous croyons en l’avenir de notre entreprise et travaillons actuellement à lever des fonds, une étape cruciale prévue tout au long de 2025.

Ce stage constitue une réelle opportunité pour vous :
Si vous démontrez votre engagement et vos compétences, un poste à responsabilités pourra vous être proposé dès que notre levée de fonds sera finalisée.

This is a remote position.

Senior AWS Cloud Administrator

Job Summary

We are seeking an experiencedAWS Cloud Administratorwith 7-8 years of overall IT experience and strong expertise in AWS Cloud infrastructure management, administration, monitoring, security, networking and cost optimization. Candidate will be responsible for managing production cloud environments, ensuring high availability, implementing security best practices, supporting cloud migrations, and driving operational excellence across AWS workloads.

Experience Required

  • 7-8 Years Overall IT Experience

  • Minimum 5+ years managing AWS production environments.

  • Experience supporting enterprise-scale cloud workloads.

  • Strong background in Linux/Windows administration, networking, security, and automation.

Key Roles & Responsibilities

  • Manage, monitor, and maintain AWS production, staging, and development environments.

  • Provision and administer AWS resources using infrastructure best practices.

  • Design and maintain highly available and fault-tolerant cloud environments.

  • Perform capacity planning, performance tuning, and resource optimization.

  • Manage multi-account AWS environments using AWS Organizations.

  • Administer EC2 instances, AMIs, Auto Scaling Groups, and Launch Templates.

  • Manage Elastic Load Balancers (ALB/NLB).

  • Configure and maintain EBS, EFS, FSx, and S3 storage services.

  • Perform storage lifecycle management and optimization.

  • Manage VPCs, Subnets, Route Tables, NAT Gateways, Internet Gateways, and Security Groups.

  • Troubleshoot network connectivity and routing issues.

  • Configure VPN, Direct Connect, Transit Gateway, and VPC Peering.

  • Implement network security and segmentation best practices.

  • Manage AWS IAM Users, Groups, Roles, and Policies.

  • Implement least-privilege access controls.

  • Configure MFA, AWS SSO, and identity federation.

  • Support security hardening and compliance requirements.

  • Review and remediate security findings.

  • Implement AWS Backup solutions.

  • Configure automated snapshots and retention policies.

  • Develop and test disaster recovery procedures.

  • Maintain backup compliance and recovery objectives (RPO/RTO).

  • Develop and maintain Infrastructure as Code solutions.

  • Automate cloud deployment and operational tasks.

  • Support CI/CD and DevOps integration initiatives.

  • Strong knowledge of ITSM process and tool – Incident ,Change ,Problem Management.

Cost Optimization & Governance

  • Monitor AWS spend using Cost Explorer and AWS Budgets.

  • Identify cost-saving opportunities and right-sizing recommendations.

  • Optimize Reserved Instances, Savings Plans, and storage costs.

jobs.description:
Vaan is a Shopify Platinum design & technology agency and the home of Brand Conversion Design.

We migrate, design, and build high performing eCommerce experiences leveraging our Brand Conversion Design framework, industry partnerships & deep eCommerce technical expertise. Solving the tension between optimization and design, we help brands make the most of their eCommerce.

About the role

Vaan partners with direct-to-consumer and B2B brands from $5M to $1B in GMV, across new builds, platform migrations, and ongoing optimization retainers. Our work spans development, design, A/B testing, and strategic roadmapping in one of the fastest-moving platform environments in commerce.

The Solutions Strategist sits between client understanding and technical execution. This is not a developer role and does not require one. It requires someone who can walk into a complex merchant environment, understand how systems connect, identify friction, and turn that into a requirements picture engineering and design can build against.

We value specificity over generalism, forward-thinking over comfort with the status quo, and partners over vendors.

Responsibilities

  • Lead technical discovery for new engagements, migrations, and major projects, surfacing the requirements others miss
  • Run structured sessions with client stakeholders across technical, marketing, and ops functions, and turn what surfaces into documentation the full team can act on
  • Translate ambiguous business needs into scoped functional and technical requirements, including an explicit account of what is out of scope and why
  • Decompose requirements into epics and stories an engineer can pick up without a follow-up conversation, working alongside the Product Owner to keep the backlog accurate as the engagement moves
  • Maintain the requirements record page by page and section by section, covering features and functions, metafields, and the apps in play, with every line traceable to scope
  • Work with Tech Leads to document architecture, data flows, and business rules, and to validate feasibility and scope before requirements become commitments
  • Build and maintain the discovery frameworks and templates the rest of the team works from
  • Translate what a client asks for into what they actually need, then identify the tool that serves it, with reasoning legible to the client, engineering, and the account team
  • Maintain working awareness of what is already implemented across our portfolio, so recommendations build on existing stack decisions instead of duplicating or contradicting them
  • Evaluate third-party tools across loyalty, search, reviews, personalization, subscriptions, and headless commerce, knowing each category well enough to ask the right questions and judge honestly
  • Recognize when someone else on the team knows a tool better than you, and pull them in early
  • Track Shopify platform updates, deprecations, and roadmap signals, and translate what changes into client guidance
  • Advise on stack composition with a focus on long-term maintainability, scalability, and cost
  • Map complex client environments across ERPs, PIMs, OMS platforms, CRM systems, and marketing stacks, including how they connect and where Shopify fits
  • Identify integration requirements, data flows, and failure points before they become project risks
  • Audit existing Shopify implementations for technical debt, architectural gaps, and unused platform capability, and articulate what should change and why
  • Understand how AI works inside the apps our clients already run. Most of the ecosystem is adding AI features across search, merchandising, personalization, support, and retention. The question is never whether the feature exists. It is whether turning it on moves a business objective this client actually has
  • Hold a working read on where AI creates genuine value in ecommerce and where it is noise, and be able to explain the difference to a client without hedging
  • Identify where AI-enabled tooling could improve conversion, retention, or operational efficiency for a client, and build the case
  • Use AI in your own delivery work: drafting specs, scripting audits, analyzing rulesets, reconciling data, roughing out wireframes to move a conversation along
  • Work as a peer to Growth Strategists. You are the reason a commercially attractive roadmap item is deliverable, or the reason it gets reshaped before it is promised to a client
  • Contribute technical context to scoping and estimation that makes the numbers more accurate
  • Keep engineering, design, and the account team working from the same requirements picture, and surface the conflict early when they are not

Qualifications

  • A track record of picking the right tool for a specific client context and being able to defend the choice to both the client and the engineers who have to live with it
  • Working familiarity with Shopify Plus across admin, metafields, theme architecture, and B2B, enough to reason about what is possible without needing to build it
  • Understanding of headless and composable architectures, and of when they are the wrong call
  • Comfort saying you do not know a tool well, and a habit of finding the person who does
  • A track record of leading discovery on complex digital projects, with documentation habits that survive contact with a deadline
  • Ability to run stakeholder sessions that surface the real requirements, meaning what clients actually need rather than what they say they want
  • Experience writing requirements engineering can execute against with minimal ambiguity, and breaking them down to a granularity a developer can pick up
  • Experience holding requirements for several clients at once without context bleeding between them
  • Exposure to platform migration from Magento, BigCommerce, or Salesforce Commerce Cloud to Shopify Plus
  • Working comfort in Figma or FigJam, Jira, and Excel. You don't need mastery. You should be able to run a session on a canvas, author a story, and keep a structured requirements sheet clean
  • Experience evaluating AI features inside tools a merchant already pays for, rather than only standalone AI products, and judging whether switching one on is worth the change
  • Comfort with rapid change. You update your position when the evidence warrants it, and you say so out loud
  • Confident in client-facing environments, able to ask hard questions diplomatically and explain technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders
  • Able to propose a compromise a client will accept, an engineer will respect, and the account team can still deliver inside the SOW
  • Strong written communication. Your requirements documents, briefs, and follow-ups are clear and trusted by the people who use them

Job Title: In-Home Nurse Practitioner or Physician Assistant Part Time - Cincinnati, OH

Job Location: Work at Home, Ohio, United States

Job Location Type: Remote

We’re building a world of health around every individual — shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger – helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time.

Do you have a passion for engaging with people and helping them on their journey to better health? Signify Health, part of CVS Health®, is seeking a Part Time Clinician (Nurse Practitioner or Physician Assistant) to provide In-Home Health Evaluations, engaging with people in the comfort of their own homes and helping bridge gaps in care.

You’ll play a critical role in building trusted relationships to make people healthier, helping bring flexible, comprehensive and personalized health evaluations right to people’s front doors.

Job highlights

The visit, which lasts about 45 minutes, allows for time to connect one-on-one and answer health questions. It includes a medication and medical history review, a physical evaluation, and, if ordered by the person’s health plan, additional diagnostic tests (i.e., diabetic eye exams, spirometry, etc.). You’ll use an iPad and an intuitive clinical workflow for each evaluation and are not required to prescribe medicine, order lab tests or alter people’s current treatment regimen.

In this role, you will:

  • Bring your heart into every visit, joining a national network of purpose-driven clinicians dedicated to improving health outcomes

  • Be part of our efforts to visit millions of people nationwide with the goal of providing connections to the right care for people’s unique needs

  • Work with Signify Health as a clinician colleague, fulfilling the requirements of the specified role

  • Be flexible to travel locally and within licensed states, as needed

  • Conduct virtual visits as needed

  • Provide all Signify Health services as indicated including Diagnostic & Preventive Services products (i.e., spirometry, DEE, bone density screening, etc.)

A Note on Our Work Environment:
As an in-home clinician, your primary workplace is the private residence of health plan members. We are dedicated to meeting health plan members where they are, wherever they call home. These environments are diverse and may present a variety of conditions. Candidates must be able to comfortably and safely perform their duties in homes that may contain household pets, secondhand smoke and other potential airborne allergens or irritants.

Why Clinicians Enjoy Working with Signify Health
“I love seeing health plan members at home. You get a better picture of their health when you see where they live.” - Erica R., PA

“At Signify Health, we have the time to help people and to truly listen to their questions and concerns. We can help guide them so they can take better care of themselves. We really can make a change in communities.” - Ali B., NP

“I like how Signify Health manages my experience. I’m just doing the clinician part of my job without all the administrative responsibilities. I have the time to provide education so people have a better understanding of their health. I can answer their questions without rushing out the door.” - Andrew K., PA

Part-time employees qualify for:

  • Select benefits (see benefits guide for details)

  • Malpractice insurance coverage (during Signify Health-related activities)

  • Supplies and other perks

Required & Preferred Qualifications (NPs and PAs)

  • Active, unrestricted license(s) in coverage area(s)

  • Board certification (required)

  • Multi-state licenses (preferred)

29.5

Time Type

Part time

Pay Range

The typical pay range for this role is:

$41.85 - $90.13

This pay range represents the base hourly rate or base annual full-time salary for all positions in the job grade within which this position falls. The actual base salary offer will depend on a variety of factors including experience, education, geography and other relevant factors.

Our people fuel our future. Our teams reflect the customers, patients, members and communities we serve and we are committed to fostering a workplace where every colleague feels valued and that they belong.

Great benefits for great people

We take pride in offering a comprehensive and competitive mix of pay and benefits that reflects our commitment to our colleagues and their families.

This part‑time position is eligible for a range of benefits and programs that support the physical, emotional, and financial well‑being of colleagues. The Behavioral Health Integration Clinician is a central member of a patient’s collaborative care team. The core team includes the patient’s medical provider and psychiatric consultant.   • Provide health behavior and social determinants of health interventions to improve functioning and improvements in medical outcomes.
  • Systematically track treatment response and monitor patients (in person, video or by telephone) for changes in clinical symptoms and treatment side effects or complications.

  • Provide or facilitate in-clinic or outside referrals to evidence-based psychosocial treatments (e.g. problem-solving treatment or behavioral activation) as clinically indicated.
  • Participate in regularly scheduled (usually weekly) caseload consultation with the psychiatric consultant and communicate resulting treatment recommendations to the patient’s medical provider.
  • Track patients follow up and clinical outcomes using the EHR. Document in-person, video and telephone encounters in the EHR and use the system and established clinical workflows to identify and re-engage patients.
  • Document patient progress and treatment recommendations in EHR and other required systems to be shared with medical providers, psychiatric consultants, and other treating providers.
  • Facilitate treatment plan changes for patients who are not improving as expected in consultation with the medical provider and the psychiatric consultant and who may need more intensive or more specialized mental health care.

Signify Health, part of CVS Health®, is seeking a Part Time Clinician (Nurse Practitioner or Physician Assistant) to provide In-Home Health Evaluations, engaging with people in the comfort of their own homes and helping bridge gaps in care.

You’ll play a critical role in building trusted relationships to make people healthier, helping bring flexible, comprehensive and personalized health evaluations right to people’s front doors.

Job highlights

The visit, which lasts about 45 minutes, allows for time to connect one-on-one and answer health questions. It includes a medication and medical history review, a physical evaluation, and, if ordered by the person’s health plan, additional diagnostic tests (i.e., diabetic eye exams, spirometry, etc.). You’ll use an iPad and an intuitive clinical workflow for each evaluation and are not required to prescribe medicine, order lab tests or alter people’s current treatment regimen.

In this role, you will:

  • Bring your heart into every visit, joining a national network of purpose-driven clinicians dedicated to improving health outcomes

  • Be part of our efforts to visit millions of people nationwide with the goal of providing connections to the right care for people’s unique needs

  • Work with Signify Health as a clinician colleague, fulfilling the requirements of the specified role

  • Be flexible to travel locally and within licensed states, as needed

  • Conduct virtual visits as needed

  • Provide all Signify Health services as indicated including Diagnostic & Preventive Services products (i.e., spirometry, DEE, bone density screening, etc.)

A Note on Our Work Environment:
As an in-home clinician, your primary workplace is the private residence of health plan members. We are dedicated to meeting health plan members where they are, wherever they call home. These environments are diverse and may present a variety of conditions. Candidates must be able to comfortably and safely perform their duties in homes that may contain household pets, secondhand smoke and other potential airborne allergens or irritants.

Why Clinicians Enjoy Working with Signify Health
“I love seeing health plan members at home. You get a better picture of their health when you see where they live.” - Erica R., PA

I have the time to provide education so people have a better understanding of their health. I can answer their questions without rushing out the door.” - Andrew K., PA

Job Title: Cybersecurity Architect

Job Location: Atlanta, GA

Job Location Type: Remote

Job Contract Type: Full-time

Company Description

About AbbVie

AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at . Follow @abbvie on LinkedIn,Facebook, Instagram, X and YouTube.


Job Description

This is a technical role responsible for executing the design, building, testing, and implementation of security systems across our environment, with a specific emphasis on endpoint security and mobility. You will work closely with other members of the Information Security team to identify potential threats and vulnerabilities and develop strategies and solutions to mitigate these risks, securing the end-user device estate and the mobile platforms through which the enterprise increasingly operates, and contributing to our overall information security strategy.

This position can be virtual anywhere in the U.S.

You will join the Business Technology Solutions (BTS) Information Security and Risk Management (ISRM) Architecture organization. Our team translates business objectives and cyber risk strategy into concrete security measures — processes, technologies, and services — across a diverse and complex infrastructure landscape, including on-premises, cloud, and X-as-a-Service models.

Responsibilities:

  • Define and evaluate security architecture for the end-user device estate — workstation and laptop hardening, EDR/endpoint protection (e.g., CrowdStrike, Defender), data protection, and configuration baselines.
  • Advise on mobility security: MDM/UEM (e.g., Microsoft Intune), mobile application management, conditional access, and BYOD posture across iOS and Android.
  • Perform Security Architecture Reviews — adjudicate submissions, align the risk and controls with the system owner, and ensure review quality.
  • Deliver Security Architecture Consulting engagements with business partners — own each engagement end to end, with timely turnaround and clear customer communication.
  • Provide Risk Evidence Review on request, partnering with Risk Management to evaluate control and mitigation effectiveness for risk owners.
  • Plan, design, build, and implement enterprise security architecture, and create relevant documentation of same.
  • Evaluate security technologies and controls across the environment — including those employed by third-party providers — developing strategies, determining which controls fit a given situation, and adapting them to business needs, risk, and the threat landscape.
  • Identify and communicate current and emerging security threats and risks; design security architecture elements and propose new or revised measures to mitigate them as they emerge.
  • Help develop solutions that balance information security needs with the needs of the business, in collaboration with team members and business and IT stakeholders.
  • Be fluent with AI concepts and incorporate AI into your daily workflows — using AI to accelerate design reviews, threat modeling, documentation, and analysis — targeting improved efficiency, quality, and speed.
  • Create reusable security-architecture artifacts — reference architectures, design patterns, security guidelines, and security positions — that scale the team's expertise beyond one-off engagements.
  • Identify recurring problems and build durable systems, patterns, and standards that solve them at the root — not only technical problems, but process and people problems too — so the same issue does not keep resurfacing.
  • Support training and mentorship of more junior employees as well as employees outside the Information Security Team, as needed.

Qualifications

Required:

  • Bachelor's Degree and 8 years of experience OR Master's Degree and 7 years of experience OR PhD and 3 years of experience.
  • Demonstrated proficiency with security controls and concepts.
  • Working knowledge of security frameworks and standards (e.g., NIST, CIS Controls, OWASP, Cloud Security Alliance).
  • Advanced knowledge of operating systems, networking protocols, systems administration, and security technologies.
  • Advanced knowledge and application of cybersecurity terminology and concepts, and foundational understanding of the cyber threat landscape and attack vectors.
  • Understanding of risk management principles and the ability to integrate them into security practices.
  • Capable of learning new concepts and processes quickly and adapting to a constantly changing environment.
  • Fluency with AI concepts and demonstrated use of AI tools to improve how you work.
  • Demonstrated critical thinking, problem solving, and analytical skills.
  • Strong organizational skills with attention to detail.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with a high level of professionalism.
  • Ability to work independently and effectively as part of a team.
  • Willingness to be available, as needed, for major and critical security issues.
  • Demonstrated skills and experience in the following tools:
    • Endpoint protection and detection (EDR/EPP), data protection, and configuration-baseline tooling.
    • Mobile device and endpoint management (MDM/UEM, e.g., Microsoft Intune), mobile application management, and conditional access.
    • Operating systems, networking protocols, systems administration, and cloud platforms (e.g., AWS, Azure).
    • Security control frameworks and the cyber threat landscape and attack vectors.
    • AI tools and AI-assisted workflows to drive speed and quality.
    • Collaboration and documentation platforms (ServiceNow ITSM, Jira, Confluence, Microsoft 365 / SharePoint)

Preferred:

  • Professional cybersecurity certifications (e.g., CISSP, SANS/GIAC, etc.) are highly desirable.

Individual compensation paid within this range will depend on many factors including geographic location, and we may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range. This range may be modified in the future. ​

  • We offer a comprehensive package of benefits including paid time off (vacation, holidays, sick), medical/dental/vision insurance and 401(k) to eligible employees.​

  • This job is eligible to participate in our long-term incentive programs. ​

Note: No amount of pay is considered to be wages or compensation until such amount is earned, vested, and determinable. The amount and availability of any bonus, commission, incentive, benefits, or any other form of compensation and benefits that are allocable to a particular employee remains in the Company's sole and absolute discretion unless and until paid and may be modified at the Company’s sole and absolute discretion, consistent with applicable law.​

Job Title: In-Home Physician Part Time - Akron

Job Location: Work at Home, Ohio, United States

Job Location Type: Remote

We’re building a world of health around every individual — shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger – helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time.

Do you have a passion for engaging with people and helping them on their journey to better health? Signify Health, part of CVS Health®, is seeking a Part Time Physician to provide In-Home Health Evaluations, engaging with people in the comfort of their own homes and helping bridge gaps in care.

You’ll play a critical role in building trusted relationships to make people healthier, helping bring flexible, comprehensive and personalized health evaluations right to people’s front doors.

Job highlights

The visit, which lasts about 45 minutes, allows for time to connect one-on-one and answer health questions. It includes a medication and medical history review, a physical evaluation, and, if ordered by the person’s health plan, additional diagnostic tests (i.e., diabetic eye exams, spirometry, etc.). You’ll use an iPad and an intuitive clinical workflow for each evaluation and are not required to prescribe medicine, order lab tests or alter people’s current treatment regimen.

In this role, you will:

  • Bring your heart into every visit, joining a national network of purpose-driven clinicians dedicated to improving health outcomes

  • Be part of our efforts to visit millions of people nationwide with the goal of providing connections to the right care for people’s unique needs

  • Work with Signify Health as a clinician colleague, fulfilling the requirements of the specified role

  • Be flexible to travel locally and within licensed states, as needed

  • Conduct virtual visits as needed

  • Provide all Signify Health services as indicated including Diagnostic & Preventive Services products (i.e., spirometry, DEE, bone density screening, etc.)

A Note on Our Work Environment:

As an in-home clinician, your primary workplace is the private residence of health plan members. We are dedicated to meeting health plan members where they are, wherever they call home. These environments are diverse and may present a variety of conditions. Candidates must be able to comfortably and safely perform their duties in homes that may contain household pets, secondhand smoke and other potential airborne allergens or irritants.

Why Clinicians Enjoy Working with Signify Health
“Many of the people I see are shocked that a physician is coming to their home to visit with them one-on-one. When you sit down and have an unhurried conversation about their health, they are impressed, happy, and understand that their health plan and care team cares about them.” - M.L., MD

“The primary care physician gets a snapshot of a person in an office setting, but with Signify Health, we see things like the number of steps to enter their home, the state of disrepair those steps may be in, and the person’s ability to function comfortably and with ease in their own home. We can make referrals to the individual’s health plan, encourage the participation of their loved ones, and ensure their PCPs are aware of their health and overall quality of life.” - C.H., MD

Part-time employees qualify for:

  • Select benefits (see benefits guide for details)

  • Malpractice insurance coverage (during Signify Health-related activities)

  • Supplies and other perks

Required & Preferred Qualifications (MDs and DOs)

  • Active, unrestricted license(s) in coverage area(s)

  • Multi-state licenses (preferred)

$105.00 - $105.00

jobs.description:
Payroll Supervisor (Full-Time, Remote)

Remote — United States | Full-Time | $65,000 – $70,000 / year

Ensemble Performing Arts is seeking a highly organized, detail-oriented, and people-focused Payroll Supervisor to join our Finance team and lead payroll operations across our growing portfolio of performing arts businesses. This role oversees the payroll team, ensures accurate and timely processing across multiple pay schedules, and safeguards payroll reporting and regulatory compliance.

This is the right fit for someone who thrives in a fast-paced, high-accountability environment, enjoys coaching a team, and takes pride in maintaining accuracy and compliance in payroll operations.

Key Responsibilities

  • Team Leadership
    • Supervise and develop payroll coordinators, setting priorities and workloads around each pay cycle
    • Review work for accuracy, provide regular feedback, and conduct performance reviews
    • Serve as the escalation point for complex payroll issues, employee inquiries, and manager questions
    • Oversee the payroll group inbox to ensure timely, accurate responses
  • Payroll Processing
    • Oversee end-to-end processing of weekly, biweekly, and semi-monthly payrolls for hourly and salaried employees
    • Review timekeeping data, overtime, shift differentials, bonuses, commissions, and retro adjustments before each run
    • Approve payroll registers, resolve discrepancies, and release payments, including direct deposits, paper checks, and off-cycle payments
    • Process garnishments, child support orders, and other deductions accurately and on schedule
    • Ensure timely, accurate processing of adjustments and final pay
  • Reporting & Reconciliation
    • Reconcile payroll to the general ledger and coordinate with Accounting on journal entries and accruals
    • Prepare payroll reports, such as labor cost, headcount, and overtime, for Finance and HR leadership
    • Maintain controls that protect confidential employee and compensation data
  • Tax & Compliance
    • Ensure compliance with the FLSA and federal, state, and local wage-and-hour, payroll tax, and reporting requirements
    • Oversee payroll tax deposits, quarterly filings (Form 941 and state equivalents), and year-end W-2/1099 processing
    • Stay current on regulatory changes and update procedures and system settings as needed
    • Support internal and external audits with clear documentation
  • Systems & Process Improvement
    • Administer the payroll system and partner with HR and IT on upgrades, integrations, and data accuracy
    • Document procedures and identify opportunities to automate and streamline processes

Who You Are

  • A people leader: you coach and develop your team, set clear priorities, and give feedback that helps people grow
  • Compliance-minded: you know multi-state payroll and wage-and-hour rules, and you stay ahead of changes
  • Accurate and detail-oriented: you catch discrepancies before payroll is released, not after
  • A process improver: you document, streamline, and automate so the team can do more, more consistently
  • Discreet and trustworthy: you protect sensitive employee and compensation data

Preferred Qualifications

  • 5+ years of experience with core payroll functions, including 2+ years in a lead or supervisory role
  • Working knowledge of multi-state payroll and wage-and-hour compliance
  • Demonstrated ability to coach, develop, and lead a team
  • Ability to manage multiple deadlines in a fast-paced environment
  • Advanced Excel skills, including pivot tables, lookups, and reconciliations
  • Excellent communication, organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills
  • Experience with Paylocity is a plus

Compensation & Benefits

The compensation range for this position is 65,000–70,000 per year, commensurate with experience. A competitive benefits package is provided, including medical, dental, and vision insurance; life and AD&D coverage; supplementary/voluntary benefit plans; Paid Time-Off; and a 401(k) with employer match.

To Apply

Please submit the following:

  • A resume
  • A brief cover letter outlining your interest in this role
  • Responses to our short questionnaire about your background. Applications without a cover letter and questionnaire response will be considered incomplete and will not be reviewed.

Diversity is a strength of our community. If you meet most but not all of the qualifications, we still encourage you to apply.

About Ensemble Performing Arts

Ensemble Performing Arts, a four-time Inc. 5000 honoree, is one of the fastest-growing platforms of independently-run performing arts schools and businesses in the United States. We are powered by passionate educators and supported by a team that believes in preserving what makes each school and business unit special. With a multi-state, multi-entity footprint and active M&A pipeline, we are committed to operational excellence and a people-first culture grounded in respect, flexibility, and shared purpose. We offer opportunities for growth and leadership in a fast-scaling organization.

Who We Are

Our mission is to empower artists by safeguarding the businesses that love them ♡. Our values include:

  • Stewardship: We are caretakers of our performing arts businesses and communities, helping them thrive by making it easy for our teams and educators to cultivate an enriching experience for the students we serve.
  • Growth: Our performing arts businesses are integral to our success, and we are committed to their professional growth. As an ever-growing partnership across the performing arts education space, we seek to increase the high-quality resources provided to our businesses and the people who run them.
  • Stagehands: Our Shared Services team runs in the background to support our businesses. By doing this, we champion students to be the real stars of the show!

To learn more about Ensemble Performing Arts, visit .

Ensemble Performing Arts is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, protected veteran status or disability status, or genetic information. Pursuant to the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers and any other state or local hiring regulations, we will consider for employment any qualified applicant, including those with arrest and conviction records, in a manner consistent with applicable law. It is unlawful in Massachusetts to require or administer a lie detector test as a condition of employment or continued employment. An employer who violates this law shall be subject to criminal penalties and civil liability.

jobs.title: RFP: Human Resource Subject Matter Lead
jobs.excerpt: About NLA and TCS New Left Accelerator (NLA) and its 501(c)(3) affiliate, The Capacity Shop (TCS), lead operational capacity-building programs that empower social justice organizations and movements to execute bold work safely.
jobs.companyName: New Left Accelerator and The Capacity Shop
jobs.description:
About NLA and TCS

New Left Accelerator (NLA) and its 501(c)(3) affiliate, The Capacity Shop (TCS), lead operational capacity-building programs that empower social justice organizations and movements to execute bold work safely. We bridge the gap between ambitious strategy and operational excellence, scaling structures and impact without sacrificing legal compliance or integrity. To achieve systemic change, organizations must use every tool in their toolbox effectively—including multi-entity structures.

Through deep collaboration with field experts, we build the financial and compliance training systems that allow movement organizations to manage risk and remain resilient. Our work is rooted in a commitment to:

  • Power Building For Systemic Change: Equipping organizations to build power to dismantle oppressive structures.
  • Operational Power: Building the "operational" capacity to execute bold work and to strategically manage risk.
  • A Multi-Entity Lens: Optimizing the diverse legal structures necessary to win critical battles.
  • Transformative Partnerships: Prioritizing those working at the intersections of race, gender, and class.

At NLA, our work is guided by a Theory of Change. We accompany organizations and movements in building sustainable, resilient ecosystems prepared to win the most ambitious fights of our time.

Overview of Project

Background

NLA and TCS develop training on a range of operations topics, focused on what multi-entity organizations need to know. We are developing foundational content for a training module for HR staff at mid-size, multi-entity social justice organizations that do election-year work. The content will focus on the HR issues specific to these organizations when they hire for organizing positions during an election cycle and then end those positions afterward.

Scope of Work

The HR Subject Matter Lead will work under the direction of the TCS, Senior Director of Training and Curriculum to develop a four-part, role-based education module for HR specialists. The module will:

  • Apply a nonprofit multi-entity Human Resources lens throughout
  • Apply a social justice lens to HR in the organizing and election year context
  • Build on existing NLA/TCS content
  • Incorporate NLA's learning frameworks and practices
  • Be customizable for state content

Deliverables and Outcomes

December 2026 through June 2027

  • Content Audit Report: An assessment of existing NLA/TCS HR content that sorts it into what can be used as is, what needs updating, and what's missing. It will include recommendations for the Content Lead.
  • Co-Design Program Line with NLA: Work with TCS and NLA staff to propose the format of the TCS HR pilot program line; consider implications for integration of content into other NLA/TCS program lines.
  • Module Design Proposal: A proposed outline for how we might break out role-based HR education modules segmenting existing content and identifying modifications or needed updates, propose for each training, learning objectives, key topics, and clarity which pre-existing source content that training will draw on and how content will hold together to create an integrated learning experience (define elements like office hours)
  • Training Materials (one set for each of the four trainings): Facilitator guides, slide decks, tools and resources and participant materials, all finalized with the NLA/TCS T&C and content team.
  • Supporting Tools & Resources: Work with content team to co-create HR focused tools, guides, and templates that go with each training in the module.
  • Delivery of Four Trainings (pilot): Conduct live training and facilitation of the module in collaboration with TCS training team; document what works and what does not for improvement.
  • Pilot Debrief and Revision Recommendations: A summary of what was learned from the pilots, with recommended changes. It will also include updated materials that reflect the changes the Content Lead approves.

Steers

  • Start with what exists. Adapt and strengthen current materials rather than redesigning by default.
  • Learn and apply the NLA/TCS competencies (Attitudes & Beliefs, Knowledge & Skills, People & Resources, Systems & Processes) as a diagnostic lens.
  • Prioritize practical application. Use realistic scenarios, decision points, and tools that participants can apply in their organizations.
  • Make distinctions clear. Identify when an issue is a routine management matter, an HR matter, or one that requires employment counsel or other specialized expertise.
  • Design for adult learners with varied levels of HR responsibility and experience. Ensure the content and guides are useful for organizations with limited HR infrastructure as well as those with dedicated HR staff.
  • Keep organizational decisions internal. The consultant will advise and develop content in partnership with staff; NLA/TCS retains final approval.
  • Keep the scope focused on content development, training delivery, and transfer. New legal research, state-by-state guidance, or broader HR consulting must be separately approved.
  • Engage in quality control process and help ensure accuracy and compliance of products

What We Are Looking For

  • 10 years HR experience within multi-entity election-cycle workforces, including employee relations, people management, HR operations, and employment compliance
  • Experience translating complex HR concepts into clear, practical training for non-HR audiences.
  • Training and curriculum development and adult-learning facilitation skills, including virtual training experience (can be public or within organizations).
  • Significant experience supporting movement-building organizations, especially 501(c)(3)s, 501(c)(4)s, campaigns, and/or PACs, with a strong understanding of shared staffing structures and multi-entity operations.
  • Ability to work with HR attorneys to translate legal advice into training content; ability to distinguish general HR education from legal advice and to flag areas requiring review by employment counsel and help manage compliance, accuracy and quality of content.
  • A collaborative working style and demonstrated ability to incorporate feedback without losing technical accuracy or instructional coherence.

Proposal Requirements

Please submit:

  • Letter of Interest (1 page maximum) that covers:
    • Your experience with multi-entity Human Resources including in an election year context.
    • Proposed approach to the scope of work and why you are best positioned to execute this work
    • A fee proposal, including your assumptions about level of effort (for example, estimated hours per deliverable)
  • Resume showing relevant experience in:
    • Human resources in the nonprofit, movement or social justice space, election-cycle settings
    • Curriculum and training development
    • Facilitation
    • Movement building
    • Multi-entity organizations (for example, 501(c)(3), 501(c)(4), and PAC structures)

Submission Information

  • Submissions will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Priority deadline is November 6, 2026
